_note: 순서(논설문) FULL set. 유형마다 passage를 다르게 paraphrase. grammar/vocab의 밑줄 어구는 해당 passage 문장에 글자 그대로 존재. blank의 blank_target, insert의 insert_sentence, implication의 underlined도 동일.

passage: Even if some aspects of spectacle can produce instinctive reactions, it primarily functions within the cultural context that shapes how observers perceive it.
Creating spectacle is not an automatic or universal feature of human culture, but rather a deliberate strategy employed across diverse societies to fulfill particular purposes.
Like a novelist who must balance genre expectations with fresh ideas, anyone crafting a spectacle must work within cultural conventions while introducing something new.
A spectacle is therefore built by embracing both the inherited traditions and the creative innovations of a given culture.
Established techniques drawn from past ceremonies and events may form the foundation, yet merely reproducing them will not produce true spectacle.
The spectacle must ultimately exceed what came before, astonishing its audience in ways that lodge it firmly in shared cultural memory.
Only by combining respectful tradition with bold originality can a spectacle achieve lasting impact and become part of the collective experience.
choices: the role of literature in shaping cultural ceremonies and festivals
how spectacle balances cultural convention with originality to create memorable impact
why instinctive reactions are more powerful than learned cultural responses
the economic benefits of staging large-scale public spectacles
how collective memory is recorded and preserved across generations
theme.explanation_ko: 스펙터클은 문화적 틀 안에서 기존 관습과 독창성을 혼합해야 지속적 영향을 남긴다는 내용. ②가 주제이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ①문학의 역할, ③본능 vs 학습, ④경제적 이익, ⑤집단 기억의 기록은 본문의 핵심 초점이 아니다.

passage: Although instinct may play a role, spectacle is fundamentally shaped by the cultural perceptions its audience brings.
Creating it is no universal impulse but a purposeful strategy tailored to the needs of a specific community.
Like the writer who obeys genre conventions yet must dazzle readers with something original, the spectacle-maker walks the same tightrope.
Working with a culture's grain means drawing on familiar conventions and fusing them with fresh invention.
Past festivals offer a toolkit, but mere imitation leaves the audience unmoved.
To etch itself into collective memory, a spectacle must do more than replicate — it must astonish.
The most enduring spectacles are those that feel both deeply familiar and thrillingly new.
choices: Ancient Roots of Cultural Festivals Around the World
Tradition Alone Is Not Enough: Crafting Spectacle That Amazes
How Literature and Performance Arts Share the Same Audience
Why Instinctive Reactions Override Cultural Learning
The Economic Power of Public Spectacles in Modern Society
title.explanation_ko: 스펙터클은 전통(관습) 위에 독창성을 더해야 진정으로 놀라운 장관이 된다는 핵심을 담은 ②가 제목으로 가장 적절하다.
title.distractor_ko: ①고대 기원, ③문학과 공연의 공통점, ④본능의 우위, ⑤경제적 힘은 본문과 거리가 있다.

passage: Spectacle operates primarily within a cultural frame and is subject to prevailing modes of perception that observers bring to bear.
Its creation is not a universal expression of culture but a strategy used by diverse peoples to address specific needs.
The task of creating spectacle has been likened to writing literature, where tradition and originality must coexist.
Spectacle is produced by working with the grain of a particular culture, blending the innovative with the established.
Past techniques may be drawn upon, but imitation is not enough.
Spectacle must also be spectacular.
A spectacle has to amaze spectators, outdoing previous efforts if it is to become part of the collective memory of those who witnessed and participated in it.
The spectacle that merely echoes what came before is already forgotten before the curtain falls.
implication.underlined: The spectacle that merely echoes what came before is already forgotten before the curtain falls.
choices: a spectacle that only imitates prior events fails to leave a lasting impression
a spectacle that ends quickly tends to be remembered more vividly
the best spectacles are those that remain unchanged across generations
audiences forget spectacles when they arrive too early to the event
repeating a spectacle many times increases its impact on collective memory
implication.explanation_ko: '이전 것을 그저 메아리처럼 반복하는 스펙터클은 막이 내리기도 전에 잊힌다'는 것은, 모방만 하는 스펙터클은 지속적인 인상을 남기지 못한다는 의미이다. ①이 정답.
implication.distractor_ko: ②빨리 끝나는 것, ③변하지 않는 것이 최고, ④일찍 도착과 관련, ⑤반복으로 효과 증가는 본문과 어긋난다.

passage: Although there may be elements that trigger instinctive response, spectacle works primarily within a cultural frame and is subject to prevailing modes of perception that observers bring to bear.

We stress that creation of spectacle is neither a universal nor even an inevitable expression of culture, but is a strategy commonly used by people from many different cultures to address specific needs.

The task of creating spectacle has been likened to creating new works of literature, where writers normally feel bound by the rules and traditions of their genre yet need to show sufficient originality to impress their audiences.
By extension, spectacle is produced by working with the grain of a particular culture, blending the innovative with the established.
Thus anyone deploying spectacle may draw on a repertoire of techniques and conventions developed from previous festivals or related activities, but imitation is not enough.
Spectacle must also be spectacular.
A spectacle has to amaze spectators, outdoing previous efforts if it is to become part of the collective memory of those who witnessed and participating in it.
grammar.explanation_ko: ⑤ 'those who witnessed and participating in it'에서, witnessed와 병렬을 이루어야 하므로 현재분사 participating이 아닌 과거형 participated로 고쳐야 한다. (who + 과거동사 witnessed and participated)
grammar.distractor_ko: ①works(주어 spectacle 단수에 호응), ②commonly used(strategy를 수식하는 과거분사), ③feel bound(feel+형용사 bound), ④blending(분사구문 능동) 모두 어법상 옳다.

vocab.explanation_ko: ⑤ 글은 스펙터클이 목격자들의 '집단(collective) 기억'에 남아야 한다고 말한다. individual(개인적인)은 글의 핵심인 공유된 사회적 기억과 반대이므로 문맥상 부적절하다.
vocab.distractor_ko: ①prevailing(지배적인), ②inevitable(불가피한), ③originality(독창성), ④innovative(혁신적인)는 모두 문맥에 적절하다.

blank.explanation_ko: 앞에서 스펙터클은 이전 노력을 능가해야 하며 관중을 놀라게 해야 한다고 했다. 목격자들의 '집단 기억(collective memory)'의 일부가 되어야 한다는 내용이 가장 자연스럽게 이어진다.
blank.distractor_ko: ①역사적 기록, ②개인적 선호, ④상업적 이익, ⑤본능적 반응은 본문이 강조하는 집단 기억과 맞지 않는다.

order.given: Although there may be elements that trigger instinctive response, spectacle works primarily within a cultural frame and is subject to prevailing modes of perception that observers bring to bear.

blocks.A: By extension, spectacle is produced by working with the grain of a particular culture, blending the innovative with the established. Thus anyone deploying spectacle may draw on a repertoire of techniques and conventions developed from previous festivals or related activities, but imitation is not enough.
blocks.B: Spectacle must also be spectacular. A spectacle has to amaze spectators, outdoing previous efforts if it is to become part of the collective memory of those who witnessed and participated in it.

The task of creating spectacle has been likened to creating new works of literature, where writers normally feel bound by the rules and traditions of their genre yet need to show sufficient originality to impress their audiences.

order.explanation_ko: 주어진 글(문화적 틀) → (C) 스펙터클은 전략이며 문학 창조에 비유 → (A) 이를 확장: 관습+혁신 혼합, 모방 부족 → (B) 결론: 장관이어야 하며 이전을 능가해야. (C)-(A)-(B) 순서가 논리적.
order.distractor_ko: (A)의 'By extension'은 (C)의 문학 비유를 전제로 하므로 (C) 뒤에 와야 한다. (B)의 'also'는 앞서 논한 조건들 위에 새 조건 추가이므로 마지막에 온다.

insert.explanation_ko: 주어진 문장(스펙터클 창조 = 문학 창조 비유: 규칙+독창성)은 ②번 뒤 문장인 '스펙터클은 전략'이라는 주장을 구체적 비유로 부연하고, 이어서 ③번의 'By extension(이를 확장하면)'이 그 비유를 확장한다. 따라서 ②가 정답.
insert.distractor_ko: 주어진 문장 없이는 ②의 '전략' 주장과 ③의 'By extension' 사이에 비유적 부연 단계가 빠져 논리 비약이 생긴다.

passage: Spectacle operates primarily within a cultural frame shaped by how observers perceive the world.
Its creation is not a universal trait of culture but a purposeful strategy meeting specific societal needs.
Like literature that must respect genre conventions yet show creativity, spectacle balances tradition with originality.
It is made by aligning with a culture's tendencies and fusing innovation with what is already familiar.

summary.summary_template: Spectacle functions within a __(A)__ framework and must combine established __(B)__ with originality to genuinely amaze audiences and enter collective memory.
summary.explanation_ko: 스펙터클은 (A)문화적(cultural) 틀 안에서 기존 (B)관습(conventions)을 독창성과 혼합해야 집단 기억으로 남는다는 내용. ①이 정답.
summary.distractor_ko: (A)는 universal/instinctive/economic이 아니라 cultural, (B)는 innovations/reactions/competitions/resources가 아니라 conventions여야 한다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.explanation_ko: 주어 Spectacle + 조동사 must + also + 동사원형 be + 보어 spectacular.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 스펙터클은 특정 문화의 흐름에 맞춰 작업함으로써, 혁신적인 것과 기존의 것을 혼합함으로써 만들어진다.
writing.answer: By extension, spectacle is produced by working with the grain of a particular culture, blending the innovative with the established.
writing.explanation_ko: 수동태 is produced + by -ing(working) + 분사구문 blending the innovative with the established.

writing.question: 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 스펙터클을 창조하는 과제는 새로운 문학 작품을 창조하는 것에 비유되어 왔다.
conditions: liken A to B의 수동태를 사용할 것
writing.answer: The task of creating spectacle has been likened to creating new works of literature.
writing.explanation_ko: 동명사구 The task of creating spectacle(주어) + has been likened to(현재완료 수동) + creating new works of literature(전치사 to의 목적어 동명사).

writing.question: 다음 밑줄 친 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: A spectacle has to amaze spectators, outdoing previous efforts if it is to become part of the collective memory of those who witnessed and participated in it.
writing.answer: 스펙터클은 관중을 놀라게 해야 하며, 그것을 목격하고 참여한 사람들의 집단 기억의 일부가 되려면 이전의 노력을 능가해야 한다.
writing.explanation_ko: has to amaze(~해야 한다) / outdoing(분사구문: 능가하면서) / if it is to become(~하려면: be to 용법) / collective memory(집단 기억) / those who witnessed and participated(목격하고 참여한 사람들).

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
writing.summary: Spectacle functions within a cultural frame and must blend established (A)___________ with originality; only by outdoing previous efforts can it become part of the (B)___________ memory of those who witnessed it.
writing.explanation_ko: (A) 이전 관습·기술의 레퍼토리를 활용한다 → conventions. (B) 목격자들의 공유된 기억 → collective(memory).

writing.context: In saying that, we stress that creation of spectacle is neither a universal nor even an ___________ expression of culture, but is a strategy commonly used by people from many different cultures to address specific needs.
writing.explanation_ko: neither A nor B 구문에서 'universal'과 병렬 관계로 스펙터클이 '불가피하지도' 않다는 의미 → inevitable(불가피한).
